doc.tool: Read a UR5e state step (TCP pose, joints, gripper, setpoint) and its camera images, main camera first.
Read every camera's intrinsics, depth availability, mount and hand-eye calibration.

camera.description: Camera name (default: the main camera; have {{cameras}})

doc.tool: Back-project one camera pixel (row, col; row 0 = top) into UR5e base coordinates through its depth, intrinsics and hand-eye calibration.

camera.description: Camera name (default: the main camera; have {{cameras}})

doc.tool: SAM3 segmentation of a camera image from the latest (or given) step. Give exactly one of a text prompt or a positive point [row, col]. On a camera with depth the mask's pixels are back-projected and world_xyz is their median base-frame point. Returns an overlay image.

delta_xyz.description: Base-frame [dx, dy, dz], m (at most {{max_move}} m per call)

doc.tool: Move the UR5e TCP by a bounded base-frame xyz delta in meters (x forward, y left, z up; at most {{max_move}} m per call); the orientation is held.
doc.code:
Translate the TCP by a base-frame delta in metres, orientation held; refused before anything moves beyond the per-call limit (--max-move and the config's limits.max_move_m) or outside the workspace. Returns ok, start/target/final_tcp_pose, final_error_m, notes.

Example:
    r = move_delta([0, 0, -0.03])  # 3 cm down, orientation held
    print(r["ok"], r["final_tcp_pose"][:3])

xyz.description: Base-frame [x, y, z], m (at most {{max_move}} m from the current pose)

rotvec.description: Orientation as an axis-angle rotation vector, rad

rpy.description: Orientation as extrinsic xyz Euler angles, rad

doc.tool: Move the UR5e TCP to an absolute base-frame pose within the per-call limits ({{max_move}} m, {{max_rotate}} rad): xyz in meters plus an orientation as rotvec (axis-angle, rad) or rpy (extrinsic xyz Euler, rad); omit both to keep the orientation.
doc.code:
Move the TCP to an absolute base-frame pose: xyz (m) and an orientation as rotvec or rpy (rad; give at most one, omit both to keep it). Refused before anything moves when the pose is further than the per-call limits from the current setpoint (--max-move, --max-rotate and the config's), outside the workspace or tilted past limits.max_tilt_rad.

Example:
    p = get_robot_state()["raw_base_state"]["tcp_pose"]
    move_pose([p[0] + 0.03, p[1], p[2]])  # absolute, within the per-call limit

delta_rpy.description: Base-frame [droll, dpitch, dyaw], rad (norm at most {{max_rotate}} rad per call)

doc.tool: Rotate the UR5e TCP by a bounded base-frame rpy delta in radians (extrinsic xyz: roll about base x, pitch about y, yaw about z; norm at most {{max_rotate}} rad per call).
doc.code:
Rotate the TCP by a base-frame roll/pitch/yaw delta in radians; refused beyond the per-call limit (--max-rotate and the config's limits.max_rotate_rad) or the tilt limit.

Example:
    rotate_delta([0, 0, 0.1])  # yaw 0.1 rad

doc.tool: Open the Robotiq gripper and wait for the fingers to settle; fingers that do not move report gripper_jammed.
doc.code:
Open gripper fully and wait for the fingers to settle; reports gripper_jammed when they did not move.

Example:
    open_gripper()

doc.tool: Close the Robotiq gripper and wait for the fingers to settle. A close that catches nothing reopens and reports grasp_empty; fingers that do not move report gripper_jammed.
doc.code:
Close gripper and wait for the fingers to settle; a close that caught nothing reopens and reports grasp_empty, fingers that did not move report gripper_jammed; object_detected tells whether it holds something.

Example:
    r = close_gripper()
    print(r["object_detected"], r.get("grasp_empty"), r.get("gripper_jammed"))

Open (open=True) or close the Robotiq gripper and wait for the fingers to settle (the low tier's gripper; open_gripper / close_gripper are the high tier's); reports object_detected, grasp_empty and gripper_jammed.

Example:
    r = set_gripper(False)
    print(r["object_detected"], r.get("grasp_empty"), r.get("gripper_jammed"))

The arm's state: TCP pose (xyz + xyzw and the UR rotation vector), joints, setpoint, gripper width (m).

Example:
    st = get_robot_state()["raw_base_state"]
    print(st["tcp_pose"][:3], st["joints"], st["gripper_position"])

Live frames per camera: images[name] RGB, depths[name] metres for cameras with depth.

Example:
    obs = get_observation()
    for name, rgb in obs["images"].items():
        print(name, rgb.shape, name in obs["depths"])

Per camera: intrinsics, depth availability, mount and hand-eye extrinsic (camera -> tcp or base).

Example:
    meta = get_camera_meta()
    K = meta["cameras"]["wrist"]["intrinsic_K"]

position.description: TCP [x, y, z] in the base frame, m

quaternion_wxyz.description: TCP orientation, wxyz (default: the current one)

doc.code:
Solve inverse kinematics for the TCP with the controller's model, seeded from the current joints (nothing moves); the solution is checked with forward kinematics.

Returns:
    {reachable, joints (6, rad) or None, max_joint_change_rad, max_joint_step_rad, reason}: one move_to_joints call may change a joint by at most max_joint_step_rad.

Example:
    p = get_robot_state()["raw_base_state"]["tcp_pose"]
    r = solve_ik([p[0], p[1], p[2] - 0.02])
    if r["reachable"]:
        move_to_joints(r["joints"])

moveJ to a joint configuration, bounded per call: each joint changes at most limits.max_joint_step_rad, the TCP stays within the per-call limits (--max-move, --max-rotate and the config's) of where it starts and inside the workspace along the path (checked with forward kinematics), at the reset's joint speed; refused whole otherwise (nothing moves). Stop halts it with stopJ.

Example:
    q = get_robot_state()["raw_base_state"]["joints"]
    q[5] += 0.1  # turn the wrist
    move_to_joints(q)
